svg.title: Local control vs tumour size
svg.desc: Schematic: each additional centimetre raises the risk of local failure after RFA (HR 1.54) while SBRT shows no detectable size effect (HR 1.21, p=0.617); at 2 cm and above the local progression risk after RFA is 3.35 times that of SBRT (Wahl 2016, retrospective). Paired points: Wahl 2-year freedom from local progression 80.2% RFA vs 83.8% SBRT; Xi 2025 randomised trial (recurrent single tumour up to 5 cm) 2-year local progression-free survival 75.8% vs 92.7%; Yoon 2020 prospective phase II SBRT 100% at 2 years; HyTEC pooled 89%. Overall survival shows no demonstrable difference.

g.text: LOCAL CONTROL × TUMOUR SIZE
Local control vs tumour size
Local control after RFA falls as tumours grow; SBRT shows no detectable size effect.
This figure is about local control, not overall survival; cohorts and endpoints differ between points.
RFA (radiofrequency ablation)
SBRT (stereotactic body radiotherapy)
The size effect (Wahl 2016 · retrospective · 224 inoperable patients; median tumour 1.8 cm RFA vs 2.2 cm SBRT)
Each extra centimetre: RFA local-failure risk ×1.54 (p=0.006); SBRT ×1.21 (p=0.617 — no detectable size effect)
At 2 cm and above: RFA local progression risk is 3.35× that of SBRT (p=0.025); resectable beyond 2 cm — BCLC favours resection
Location too: RFA local failure 48% beside large vessels vs 7% elsewhere (Lu 2003); periportal aggressive recurrence 15% vs 3.7% overall (Kang 2015)
% (locally controlled / free of local progression, as each study defines it)
Wahl 2016 · retrospective (US · inoperable)
2-year freedom from local progression (FFLP)
Xi 2025 · randomised trial (recurrent single tumour ≤5 cm · single centre, China)
2-year local progression-free survival (HR 0.45, p=0.014)
Yoon 2020 · prospective phase II (≤5 cm, median 1.3 cm · single arm)
2-year local control — no RFA comparator
HyTEC 2021 · pooled analysis (431 primary liver tumours · single arm)
2-year local control (93% at 1 year, 86% at 3)
Overall survival: no demonstrable difference — do not read this figure as 'SBRT is better across the board'
Wahl 2-yr OS 53% vs 46% (similar); matched NCDB favoured RFA at 5 yr (29.8% vs 19.3%, liver function unrecorded); meta-analysis: none at 3/5 yr
Kim 2020 (retrospective, 7 Asian centres): SBRT arm started far worse (BCLC B–C 65% vs 16%) yet 3-yr local recurrence was lower (21.2% vs 27.9%)
Schematic, redrawn from Wahl 2016, Xi 2025, Yoon 2020, Ohri 2021 (HyTEC), Kim 2020, Lu 2003, Kang 2015 and BCLC 2022
Cohorts, designs and endpoints differ — points are not directly comparable
